title: Theophilus negative-form destruction and surviving cast constructor
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. The complete cached Theophilus I.1-I.9 source distinguishes material preparation, a form or mold, a newly introduced filling material, destruction of the outer form, and a surviving image/cast. A finite constructor can therefore preserve method continuity while changing physical identity. This is materially different from named color/layer reference and does not assign any target word.

source.work: Theophilus, De diversis artibus, Liber I, chapters I.1-I.9
source.edition: Robert Hendrie 1847, bounded connected source section; exact edition and witness limits remain those recorded in the packet.
source.source_limit: The source describes painting preparation and image-making operations; it is not claimed as a Voynich Vorlage or as proof of a target material identity.

constructor.evaluation_order: PREPARE -> FORM_NEGATIVE -> FILL -> BREAK -> CAST -> APPLY. The same method or boundary may recur, but a method recurrence never merges batch, shell and cast identities.
constructor.consequence: The outer form can be destroyed while the later image/cast remains available for application or inspection. Thus a repeated operation can preserve boundary or method but must change physical identity from SHELL to CAST; a later reference to the surviving result cannot refer back to the destroyed shell without an explicit identity edge.
constructor.rival: R-FUSE identifies form, filling and final cast as one persistent batch. It predicts that BREAK removes the only result and that a later cast reference cannot survive destruction. R-LAYER, the nearest named-color/layer reading, treats every recurrence as a deposited pigment layer and has no destructive shell consequence.
constructor.falsifier: Reject if the complete owned source trace lacks a destruction step, if the supposed cast is only a second layer with no separate physical identity, or if the target-side construction needs a shell/cast distinction that no written component, whole residual or context can carry. Unknown material names remain variables; no target form is assigned a metal or image.
constructor.source_content_consequence: The operator system predicts an observable polarity change: before BREAK the boundary belongs to a removable shell; after BREAK it belongs to the surviving cast/image. This differs from a same-material layer model even when method and locus names recur.

predecessors.limit: Theophilus named color/reference and deposited-layer structure, but it does not model destructive form versus surviving cast identity.
Generic transformation identity does not provide the shell-destruction and survivor operator sequence.
Material transformation remains a broad predecessor; this card adds a typed physical polarity and explicit destruction consequence.
